content: 1. The immunosuppressive effects of certain drugs, including etrasimod, may increase the risk of infection. Avoid or consider alternative medications. The additive immune system effects of etrasimod in combination with antineoplastic, immune-modulating, or non-corticosteroid immunosuppressive therapies have not been studied. Co-administration during and in the weeks following etrasimod administration should be avoided. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; consider alternative methods if available. 3. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Estrogens may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 5. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 6. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor closely. 7. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; consider alternative methods if available. 9. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternative methods if available. 10. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Monitor closely. 11. Iloperidone increases the levels of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 12. Imatinib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 15. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 16. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 17. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 19. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid co-administration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect. 21. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Combination oral contraceptives have been shown to significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. 23. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 24. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 25. Lesinurad decreases the effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Use additional methods of nonhormonal contraception. Do not rely on hormonal contraception alone when taking lesinurad. 26. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of liraglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Medroxyprogesterone may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; consider alternative methods if available. 31. Maitake mushroom increases the effects of medroxyprogesterone by pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor closely. Maitake mushroom has anti-tumor effects based on animal and in vitro research. 32. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Mavacamten may decrease systemic exposures of ethinyl estradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method not affected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add nonhormonal contraception during co-administration and for 4 months after the last mavacamten dose. 33. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of metformin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Mitotane decreases the levels of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 36. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, which may lead to increased CYP enzyme activity. Monitor for decreased systemic levels of narrow therapeutic/sensitive CYP substrates affected by CYP inducers after initiating nemolizumab. Dosage modification may be needed. 40. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 55. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 56. Siponimod and medroxyprogesterone both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider the half-life and mode of action of drugs with prolonged immune effects to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 57. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible. 58. Stiripentol affects medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting and inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Stiripentol is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 59. Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of medroxyprogesterone by receptor binding competition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Sugammadex may bind to progestogen, reducing progestogen exposure. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients must use additional nonhormonal contraception for the next 7 days. 60. Medroxyprogesterone decreases levels of taurine by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitor closely. 61. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
